html:
Mohawk (Kalapuya) is a band of the Kalapuya people who lived in the valley of the Mohawk River, a branch of the McKenzie, near today's Springfield in Oregon. They are not related to the Mohawk of New York; the name is a local place name.

The Kalapuya lived in the Willamette Valley, gathering camas roots and acorns and hunting deer, and burned the valley floor each year to keep it open. Disease in the 1830s killed most of them. In 1855 the Kalapuya bands signed the Willamette Valley Treaty, and in 1856 the survivors were moved to the Grand Ronde Reservation, where their descendants are part of the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde. Other bands include the Chemapho and Santiam.
